paper.title: Only Pay for What Is Uncertain: Variance-Adaptive Thompson Sampling

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian Gaussian bandit with known heterogeneous reward variances
unmapped: Reward variances are arm-dependent (heterogeneous across arms) and known to the learner
Prior on means is independent Gaussian N(mu_0, diag(sigma_0^2)) with known parameters
settings.definition_quote: When reward variances are known: The bandit instance $(\bmu,\bsigma)$ is generated as follows. The mean arm rewards are sampled from a Gaussian distribution, $\bmu \sim P_0 = \cN(\bmu_0, \diag{\bsigma_0^2})$ ... Both $\bmu_0$ and $\bsigma_0^2$ are assumed to be known by the agent. The reward variances $\bsigma^2$ are also known.

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian Gaussian bandit with unknown heterogeneous reward variances (Gaussian-Gamma prior)
unmapped: Variances are heterogeneous across arms (fixed over time), not across rounds
Joint Gaussian-Gamma prior NG(mu_0, kappa_0, alpha_0, beta_0) on (mean, precision) of each arm, parameters known
settings.definition_quote: for any arm $i$, the mean and variance of its rewards are sampled as $(\mu_i, \sigma_i^{-2}) \sim NG(\mu_{0, i}, \kappa_{0, i}, \alpha_{0, i}, \beta_{0, i})$, where $(\bmu_0, \bkappa_0, \balpha_0, \bbeta_0)$ are known prior parameters.

symbols.sigma_0i: prior standard deviation of the mean reward of arm i
symbols.sigma_i: known reward standard deviation of arm i

conditions: mu ~ N(mu_0, diag(sigma_0^2)) with known prior parameters
rewards x_{t,i} ~ N(mu_i, sigma_i^2) with known sigma_i
tuning: delta > 0 is a free analysis parameter (not used by the algorithm)

source.label: thm:bayes_known
source.quote: Consider the above setting. Then for any $\delta > 0$, the Bayes regret of Gaussian TS is bounded as: R_n \leq \sum_{i = 1}^K\sqrt{\frac{2 \sigma_{0,i}^2}{\pi}} n \delta + \sqrt{2n} \sqrt{\sum_{i =1}^K\sigma_i^2\Big(\log(1 + n\sigma_{0,i}^{2}\sigma_i^{-2}) + \sigma_{0,i}^{2}\sigma_i^{-2}\Big)\log(1/\delta)}.

results.notes: Bayes regret over prior on means. delta is an analysis parameter; with delta=1/n gives O~(sqrt(n sum sigma_i^2 log(1+n sigma_0i^2/sigma_i^2)) + sqrt(n sum sigma_0i^2)). Algorithm does not use n, so anytime.

symbols.alpha_0i: prior Gamma shape for the precision of arm i
symbols.beta_0i: prior Gamma rate for the precision of arm i
symbols.kappa_0i: prior precision scaling of the mean of arm i in the Gaussian-Gamma prior

conditions: alpha_{0,i} >= 1 for all arms (proof uses alpha_{0,i} > 1)
(mu_i, sigma_i^{-2}) ~ NG(mu_0i, kappa_0i, alpha_0i, beta_0i) with known prior parameters
tuning: delta > 0 is a free analysis parameter (not used by the algorithm)

source.label: thm:bayes_unknown2
source.quote: Consider the above setting and let $\alpha_{0,i }\geq 1$ for all arms $i \in [K]$. Then for any $\delta > 0$, the Bayes regret of \varts is bounded as: $R_n \leq C\sqrt{n \log(1 / \delta)} + \delta C \sqrt{\frac{nK}{2\pi}}\,,$ where $C^2 = \sum_{i = 1}^K \frac{\beta_{0,i}}{\alpha_{0,i} - 1} \biggn{ \frac{2}{\kappa_{0,i}} + \frac{0.5}{\kappa_{0,i}(\alpha_{0,i}-1)} + 5\log\Big(1 + \frac{n}{\kappa_{0,i}}\Big) }$ is a constant dependent on prior parameters.

results.notes: C inlined as sqrt of C^2. Stated condition alpha_0i >= 1 makes the bound undefined at alpha_0i = 1; proof assumes > 1. Proof's final constant differs somewhat from the theorem statement; recorded the theorem statement.
